title: The Google Email That Came Before Ecosia
thinker: Rabbi Eleazar ben Azariah (in Pirkei Avot)
conflicts: Google ended the Forestle partnership 'after a few days' (taz 2010) or 'a few weeks' (Volksstimme 2019); the contemporary GoogleWatchBlog post of 29 August 2008 puts the email about three weeks after the 5 August launch, so the story says late August. Google's reason is disputed (click incentives vs not supporting non-profits); the story gives Google's stated reason and attributes Kroll's 'pretext' suspicion to him. Donation basis varies (80% of ad revenue in 2010, 80% of profits later); the story uses the contemporary taz figure. Tharawat's claim that the 'Forestle' idea dates from late 2009 contradicts the 2008 launch and is not used.
notes: Told as the founding of Ecosia framed by the earlier Forestle setback (Google's cut-off, the Yahoo deal) so the decision and what Kroll knew are documented. German-language quotations are paraphrased, not quoted. Company field is 'Ecosia (preceded by Forestle)'.
